A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical study. Their complete main texts and Appendix A are readable, and corresponding definitions, theorems, proofs, and presentation elements can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports mathematical definitions, bounds, and proofs, including Appendix A, but no original empirical results.

after.justification: V3 remains entirely theoretical. Its added graph illustration and appendix derivations are mathematical constructions, not experiments or data analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions analyze the same message-passing architecture with rationally weighted ReLU MLPs and optional graph readout. The revised aggregation classes and assumptions change the theoretical analysis, without introducing a new model or computational procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for training or evaluation. The extension from constant to Boolean graph features concerns theorem domains, not empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Color Refinement remains the analytical reference, and neither version evaluates empirical baselines. The added activation-function citation and mean-versus-sum conjecture do not introduce comparator experiments.

E3.justification: Neither version contains empirical evaluation protocols, metrics, splits, or training budgets. Revised graph constructions and representation assumptions belong to the theoretical analysis.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies. The added graph example illustrates the revised combinatorial proof.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, and statistical tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured performance or empirical qualitative outcomes. Changes to analytical bounds and mathematical findings are covered under T1.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 replaces the earlier output-size-only logarithmic/sublinear framework with logarithmic conditions controlling both output size and common denominators. Theorem 3.8 extends the domain to Boolean features but drops the sublinear/subexponential cases of v1 Theorem 3.7. New aggregation lemmas and revised MLP/information-complexity proofs substantially change the argument; Remark A.1 sketches an exponential bound for mean aggregation. The CR construction changes from 2n+1 to 2n+3 vertices, adds two leaves, replaces binomial(2n-1, n-1) with binomial(2n, n), and removes the diameter-two restriction.

C1.justification: The polynomial distinguishing-power bound and asymptotic separation from two CR iterations remain, but their claimed coverage changes substantially. V3 extends feature coverage, excludes arithmetic mean from the logarithmic class, and removes the sublinear/subexponential contribution. It also corrects graph-count growth from doubly exponential to super-exponential.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the connection between approximation and distinguishability using a 2ε separation. Section 4 newly conjectures that mean aggregation could distinguish super-polynomially many graphs despite being approximable by sum aggregation, explaining the role of arbitrarily close outputs. Remark 3.7 also restricts extensions beyond ReLU by requiring common-denominator control.

D1.justification: Section 2 newly specifies reduced-fraction representations, separately encoding numerators and denominators with logarithmic-length integer encodings, and assumes computations use this representation. V1 only refers to rational bit length. This adds computational representation detail; neither version supplies implementation or execution information.

R1.justification: V3 adds Khalife and Basu (2023) and discusses its activation-function results relative to computability assumptions. Hardy (1999) and Hanson (1972) are added to support denominator-growth arguments. Most references and the broader research positioning remain.

P1.justification: The four-section organization and Appendix A remain. V3 edits the abstract and introduction, adds an Encoding and Bit-Length subsection and explanatory passages, moves the CR construction proof into the main text, and moves the information-counting proof into the appendix. Much of the surrounding exposition is retained.

P2.justification: V3 replaces the dense two-column format with a document-wide single-column layout, changing typography, headings, equation arrangement, spacing, and reference presentation. It also adds Figure 1 illustrating the revised CR construction. Neither version contains tables.

improvement.justification: V1 includes mean aggregation in its polynomial-bound class without controlling rational denominators. V3 introduces denominator-aware conditions and proofs, explicitly excludes mean, revises the CR counting construction, and corrects the graph-growth claim. These changes substantially improve the central contribution's defensibility and scope transparency, despite losing the sublinear extension. Local proof errors remain, including Lemma A.2's inconsistent O(log n) conclusion after defining n as input bit length.
